paragraphs: Avtulmas (meaning Avtalyon, Mishnah, Chagigah 2:2; Eduyot 1:3, 5:6), head of the court, descended from Sennacherib (as stated in Gittin and Sanhedrin). Shemayah was his colleague (see there). Shimon ben Shetach and Yehudah ben Tabbai were their teachers (Avot, chapter 1). Shalshelet Hakkabbalah, 5b, writes that they received from Yehoshua ben Perachyah and Shimon ben Shetach. This is incorrect, for they did not receive from Yehoshua ben Perachyah. Hillel and Shammai were his students. Being converts, they could not pronounce he and said “in” instead of “hin.” They were permitted to judge Israel because their mothers were Israelites. A ruling was found in Rome bearing Avtalyon’s name from when he was uncircumcised (Shalshelet Hakkabbalah 25b). In their time: Akavya ben Mahalalel (see there), Admon, Chanan, and the sons of Beteira. Maimonides’ statement that Rabbi Meyasha was in their time does not appear correct. Yehudah ben Dortai was in their time (see there). They did not live long afterward—only six years (see part I, year 3722). G.A.Y. writes: in Gush Chalav are buried Avtalyon and Shemayah, Rabbi Yitzchak of Gush Chalav, and Rabbi Meir the miracle-worker. I do not know who these last two are. (Adrammelech and Sharezer, Sennacherib’s sons, because they killed their father [II Kings 18; Chelek 96], came from the reincarnation of Shemayah and Avtalyon [Gilgulei Neshamot]. Aristotle was a spark of Avtalyon, who taught unsuitable students who became Sadducees. Aristotle too was of their aspect; therefore he eventually repented and was reincarnated in Antoninus, who learned from our holy master [G.N., end of the book; Chesed LeAvraham, spring 5, stream 25]. See part I, year 3061: Zechariah’s soul was reincarnated in him.)
